carousels.name: Monday of week 3: NNN gets boring

slides.title: Week 3 without p*rn isn't hard. [[It's boring. That's the danger.]]
slides.sub: Many people say boredom, not urges, is what ends their streak.

slides.title: The excitement is [[gone]]
slides.body: No more "Day 1 energy." No milestone close. Just ordinary days. That's when p*rn starts to look interesting again.

slides.title: Boredom wants a [[hit]]
slides.body: An empty Monday evening is p*rn's best opportunity. Don't leave it empty.

slides.title: Boring is [[good]]
slides.body: Boring means p*rn isn't running your life anymore. Learn to sit with ordinary — that's recovery.

slides.title: Beat [[week 3]]
items: Start one new challenge this week.
Train harder than last week.
Book 2 plans with people.
Stop counting days obsessively — live them.

carousels.name: 7 signs you're actually ready for Day 30

slides.title: 7 signs you'll stay p*rn-free [[after November ends.]]
slides.sub: Finishing NNN is one thing. Staying free is another.

slides.title: Signs [[1–4]]
items: You've stopped counting down to Dec 1.
You know why you used p*rn in the first place.
Your evenings feel full, not empty.
You've told at least one person.

slides.title: Signs [[5–7]]
items: The blocker is staying on after November.
You've set a goal beyond 30 days.
You'd feel genuinely disappointed going back to p*rn.

slides.title: Missing [[some]]?
slides.body: You have 14 days to build them. Many people who relapse on Dec 1 never planned for Dec 2.

slides.title: Plan the [[after]].
slides.body: Write down what December looks like without p*rn. Routines. Goals. People. Make the plan now while you're strong.

carousels.name: It's not a phase. It's 7 years.

slides.title: "My p*rn habit is just a phase." [[You've been in this phase for years.]]
Do the [[math]]
slides.body: When did you first start watching p*rn regularly? 13? 15? If you're 22 now, that "phase" is 7–9 years old.

slides.title: Phases [[end]]
slides.body: Haircuts, music taste, hobbies — those are phases. They change on their own. A p*rn habit that's lasted years isn't going anywhere by itself.

slides.title: Call it what it [[is]]
slides.body: A long-term pattern. Possibly an addiction. Naming it honestly is the first step to changing it.

slides.title: Stop [[waiting]]
items: Count your years honestly.
Accept it won't stop on its own.
Take one real action today — block p*rn.
Get support for a long-term pattern.

slides.title: Nearly [[1 in 12 adults]] screened positive for compulsive sexual behavior.
slides.sub: And for many, p*rn is at the center of it.

slides.title: Screened [[positive]]
slides.body: A JAMA Network Open study (2018) found 8.6% of 2,325 adults met the clinical screening cut-off for compulsive sexual behavior — which often includes compulsive p*rn use.

slides.title: Look at your [[contacts]]
slides.body: If you have 100 people in your phone, statistically several could be struggling with compulsive sexual behavior — often p*rn. Most will never say it out loud.

slides.title: Screening ≠ [[diagnosis]]
slides.body: The researchers used a screening tool — a positive result means "talk to a professional," not a final label. But it's a signal worth taking seriously.

slides.title: Think it's [[you]]?
items: Be honest about how much p*rn you watch.
Notice failed attempts to stop.
Talk to a professional for a real assessment.
Use support while you figure it out.

slides.title: 10 small wins people notice [[in their first month without p*rn.]]
slides.sub: Check off the ones you've already felt.

slides.title: Wins [[1–4]]
items: Going to bed without the 2 AM scroll.
Waking up without guilt.
Looking people in the eye more easily.
Finishing a task without escaping to p*rn.

slides.title: Wins [[5–7]]
items: Saying no to an urge — and feeling proud.
Having nothing to hide on your phone.
Feeling present with friends or a partner.

slides.title: Wins [[8–10]]
items: More energy for training or work.
Trusting yourself a little more.
Realizing you don't need p*rn to get through a hard day.

slides.title: Small wins [[stack]].
